explanation: A right or property transferred from one generation to the next, often through family ties.
A historical region in the Middle East that includes parts of present-day Israel, Palestine, Lebanon, and Jordan. God promised this land to Abraham's descendants.
An ancient Semitic people who lived in Moab, an area east of the Dead Sea and the Jordan River.
An ancient Semitic people who lived in Edom, a region south of the Dead Sea and west of the Arabah desert.
King of the Amorites who ruled over Heshbon, mentioned in Deuteronomy 2. The Israelites fought against him and conquered his land.
King of Bashan, mentioned in Deuteronomy 2. He was defeated by the Israelites during their journey toward Canaan.
A term for the Jewish people, descendants of Jacob (also called Israel), son of Isaac and grandson of Abraham.
